source_text: Disciplina custos spei, retinaculum fidei, dux itineris salutaris, fomes ac nutrimentum bonae indolis, magistra virtutis, facit in Christo manere semper ac jugiter Deo vivere et ad promissa coelestia et ad divina praemia pervenire. Hanc et sectari salubre est, et aversari ac negligere lethale. In Psalmis loquitur Spiritus sanctus: Continete disciplinam, ne forte irascatur Dominus, et pereatis a via recta, cum exarserit cito ira ejus super vos. Et iterum: Peccatori autem dixit Deus. Ad quid exponis justificationes meas, et assumis testamentum meum per os tuum? Tu autem odisti disciplinam et abjecisti sermones meos retro. Et denuo legimus: Disciplinam qui abjicit, infelix est. Et de Salomone mandata Sapientiae monentis accepimus: Fili, ne neglexeris disciplinam Domini, nec defeceris ab eo correptus; quem enim diligit Deus corripit. Si autem Deus quem diligit corripit et ad hoc corripit ut emendet, fratres quoque, et maxime sacerdotes, non oderunt sed diligunt eos quos corripiunt ut emendent. quando et Deus per Hieremiam ante praedixerit et tempora nostra significaverit dicens: Et dabo vobis pastores secundum cor meum, et pascent vos pascentes cum disciplina. Quod si in Scripturis sanctis frequenter et ubique disciplina praecipitur, et fundamentum omne religionis ac fidei de observatione ac timore profiscitur, quid cupidius appetere, quid magis velle ac tenere nos convenit, quam ut, radicibus fortius fixis, et domiciliis nostris super petram robusta mole solidatis, inconcussi ad procellas et turbines saeculi stemus, ut ad Dei munera per divina praecepta veniamus, considerantes pariter ac scientes quod templa Dei sint membra nostra, ab omni faece contagionis antiquae lavacri vitalis sanctificatione purgata, nec violari ea aut pollui fas sit, quando qui violat et ipse violetur. Eorum nos templorum cultores et antistites sumus. Serviamus illi cujus esse jam coepimus. Paulus in Epistolis suis dicit quibus nos ad curricula vivendi per divina magisteria formavit: Non estis vestri. Empti enim estis pretio magno. Clarificate et portate Deum in corpore vestro Clarificemus et portemus Deum puro et mundo corpore et observatione meliore; et qui per sanguinem Christi redempti sumus, per omnia servitutis obsequia Redemptoris imperio pareamus, demusque operam ne quid immundum et profanum templo Dei inferatur, ne offensus sedem quam inhabitat derelinquat. Sospitantis Domini verba sunt et docentis, curantis pariter et monentis: Ecce, inquit, sanus factus es, jam noli peccare, ne quid tibi deterius fiat. Dat vivendi tenorem, dat innocentiae legem, postquam contulit sanitatem; nec habenis liberis et solutis vagari postmodum patitur, sed ipsis potius quibus sanatus fuerat mancipato gravius comminatur, quod sit scilicet minor culpa deliquisse ante cum necdum nosses disciplinam Dei, nulla sit venia ultra delinquere postquam Deum nosse coepisti. Et quidem hoc tam viri quam mulieres, tam pueri quam puellae, sexus omnis atque omnis aetas observet, et curet, pro religione et fide quam Deo debet, ne quod sanctum et purum de Domini dignatione percipitur, minus sollicito timore teneatur. Nunc nobis ad virgines sermo est; quarum quo sublimior gloria est, major et cura est. Flos est ille ecclesiastici germinis, decus atque ornamentum gratiae spiritalis, laeta indoles, laudis et honoris opus integrum atque incorruptum, Dei imago respondens ad sanctimoniam Domini, illustrior portio gregis Christi. Gaudet per illas atque in illis largiter floret Ecclesiae matris gloriosa foecunditas; quantoque plus copiosa virginitas numero suo addit, tanto plus gaudium matris augescit. Ad has loquimur, has adhortamur affectione potius quam potestate; non quod, extremi et minimi et humilitatis nostrae admodum conscii, aliquid ad censuram licentiae vindicemus, sed quod, ad sollicitudinem magis cauti, ptus de diaboli infestatione timeamus. Neque enim inanis haec cautio est et vana formido quae ad salutis viam consulit, quae Dominica et vitalia praecepta custodit, ut quae se Christo dicaverint, et a carnali concupiscentia recedentes tam carne quam mente se Deo voverint, consumment opus suum magno praemio destinatum, nec ornari jam aut placere cuiquam nisi domino suo studeant, a quo et mercedem virginitatis expectant, dicente ipso: Non omnes capiunt verbum, sed illi quibus datum est. Sunt enim spadones qui ex utero matris sic nati sunt, et sunt spadones qui coacti sunt ab hominibus, et sunt spadones qui se ipsos castraverunt propter regnum coelorum. Denuo quoque per hanc Angeli vocem continentiae munus ostenditur, virginitas praedicatur: Hi sunt qui cum mulieribus se non coinquinaverunt. Virgines enim permanserunt. Hi sunt qui sequuntur Agnum quocumque ierit. Neque enim tantum masculis continentiae gratiam Dominus repromittit et feminas praeterit, sed, quoniam femina viri portio est et ex eo sumpta atque formata est, in Scripturis fere omnibus ad protoplastum Deus loquitur, quia sunt duo in carne una et in masculo simul significatur et femina.
pass_a_gloss: Discipline is the guardian of hope, the restraint of faith, the leader of the path of salvation, the nourishment of good character, the teacher of virtue, it makes us always remain in Christ and live for God and attain the heavenly promises and divine rewards. It is healthy to follow this and lethal to turn away from and neglect it. The Holy Spirit speaks in the Psalms: Hold on to discipline, lest the Lord become angry and you perish from the straight path, when his anger burns quickly over you. And again: To the sinner God said, why do you explain my justifications and take my covenant on your mouth? You hate discipline and reject my words behind. And we read again: Whoever rejects discipline is unhappy. And from Solomon's wise commands we have received: My son, do not neglect the discipline of the Lord, nor fail when he corrects you; for God corrects whom he loves. If God corrects whom he loves and corrects to amend, brothers also, and especially priests, do not hate but love those they correct to amend. When God also foretold through Jeremiah and indicated our times, saying: I will give you shepherds according to my heart, and they will feed you, feeding with discipline. If in the holy Scriptures discipline is frequently and everywhere commanded, and the foundation of all religion and faith proceeds from observation and fear, what should we more eagerly desire, what should we more want and hold, than that, with roots more firmly fixed, and our houses solidly founded on a strong rock, we stand unshaken against the storms and whirlwinds of the world, so that we may come to God's gifts through divine commands, considering and knowing that our bodies are temples of God, purified from all the filth of ancient contamination by the sanctification of the living water, and it is not right to violate or pollute them, since whoever violates them is also violated. We are the cultivators and priests of these temples. Let us serve him whose we have begun to be. Paul says in his Epistles, by which he formed us for the courses of living through divine teachings: You are not your own, for you were bought with a great price. Clarify and carry God in your body. Let us clarify and carry God with a pure and clean body and better observation; and we who were redeemed through the blood of Christ, let us obey the command of the Redeemer through all the services of servitude, and let us give attention lest anything unclean and profane be brought into the temple of God, lest the Lord, being offended, abandon the seat he inhabits. The words of the Lord who saves and teaches are: Behold, you have been healed, do not sin anymore, lest something worse happen to you. He gives the tenor of living, gives the law of innocence, after he granted health; and he does not allow us to wander afterwards with free and loose reins, but rather threatens more severely those who were healed, because it is a smaller fault to have sinned before when you did not yet know the discipline of God, there is no forgiveness for sinning afterwards when you have begun to know God. And indeed, this should be observed and cared for by men and women, boys and girls, every sex and every age, for the religion and faith they owe to God, lest what is holy and pure, received from the Lord's dignity, be held with less solicitous fear. Now our speech is to virgins; whose glory is more sublime, their care is also greater. They are the flower of the ecclesiastical germ, the ornament of spiritual grace, a joyful character, a work of praise and honor, whole and uncorrupted, the image of God responding to the Lord's holiness, a more illustrious part of Christ's flock. The glorious fertility of the Church mother rejoices and flourishes abundantly through them; and the more numerous virginity adds to its number, the more the mother's joy increases. We speak to them, we exhort them with affection rather than power; not because, being extremely and minimally and humbly conscious, we claim anything for the censor of license, but because, being more cautious in solicitude, we fear the devil's temptation. For this caution is not empty and vain fear which consults the path of salvation, which keeps the Lord's and vital commands, so that those who have dedicated themselves to Christ, and receding from carnal concupiscence, have vowed themselves to God as much in body as in mind, may consummate their work destined for a great reward, and may not strive to be adorned or please anyone except their Lord, from whom they also expect the reward of virginity, he himself saying: Not all receive the word, but those to whom it is given. For there are eunuchs who were born so from their mother's womb, and there are eunuchs who were made so by men, and there are eunuchs who castrated themselves for the kingdom of heaven. Again, through the voice of the Angels, the gift of continence is shown, virginity is preached: These are those who have not defiled themselves with women. For they have remained virgins. These are those who follow the Lamb wherever he goes. For the Lord does not promise the grace of continence only to males and pass over females, but since the woman is a part of the man and was taken and formed from him, in almost all the Scriptures God speaks to the first-formed man, because the two are one flesh and the woman is signified in the man.

pass_b_english: Discipline guards hope, restrains faith, leads the way to salvation, feeds and strengthens good character, and teaches virtue; it keeps us always in Christ, makes us live for God, and brings us to the heavenly promises and divine rewards. To follow it is healthy; to turn away or neglect it is lethal. The Holy Spirit says in the Psalms: "Hold fast to discipline, lest the Lord become angry and you perish from the straight path when his wrath burns quickly against you" (Psalm 2:12). And again: "To the sinner God said, 'Why do you recite my statutes and take my covenant on your lips? For you hate discipline and cast my words behind you.'" And we read again: "Whoever rejects discipline is unhappy." From Solomon's wise commands we have received: "My son, do not neglect the Lord's discipline or lose heart when he corrects you; for the Lord corrects those he loves" (cf. Proverbs 3:11-12). Since God corrects those he loves in order to amend them, brothers and especially priests must not hate but love those they correct so that they may be amended. When God foretold through Jeremiah and marked our times, he said: "I will give you shepherds after my own heart, and they shall feed you with discipline" (Jeremiah 3:15). If discipline is commanded frequently and everywhere in the holy Scriptures, and the whole foundation of religion and faith springs from observance and fear, what should we more eagerly desire, what should we more want and hold, than that our roots be fixed more firmly and our houses built solidly on rock, so that we stand unshaken against the storms and whirlwinds of the world? Thus we come to God's gifts through his divine commands, knowing that our bodies are temples of God, cleansed from all the filth of ancient contamination by the sanctification of living water (1 Corinthians 6:19-20). It is not right to violate or pollute them, for whoever violates them will himself be violated. We are the cultivators and priests of these temples. Let us serve the One whose we have begun to be.

Paul says in his Epistles, by which he shaped us for the course of life through divine teaching: "You are not your own; you were bought with a great price. Glorify God in your body" (1 Corinthians 6:19-20). Let us glorify and carry God in a pure and clean body and with better observance. We who were redeemed through Christ's blood must obey the Redeemer's command through every service of our bondage, and take care that nothing unclean or profane enters God's temple, lest the Lord, offended, abandon the dwelling he inhabits. The words of the Lord who saves and teaches, who heals and warns, are these: "See, you are well; sin no more, lest something worse happen to you" (John 5:14). He gives the rule of life, the law of innocence, after granting health; he does not allow us to wander afterwards with loose reins, but threatens more severely those he has healed. For it is a smaller fault to have sinned before knowing God's discipline, but there is no forgiveness for sinning after we have come to know God. This must be observed and kept by men and women, boys and girls, every sex and every age, for the religion and faith they owe God, so that what is holy and pure, received from the Lord's goodness, is not held with less careful reverence.

Now our address is to virgins; the more sublime their glory, the greater the care they need. They are the flower of the Church's seed, the ornament of spiritual grace, a joyful nature, a work of praise and honor whole and incorrupt, the image of God answering to the Lord's holiness, a more illustrious portion of Christ's flock. The glorious fruitfulness of mother Church rejoices and flourishes abundantly through them; the more numerous virginity becomes, the more the mother's joy increases. We speak to them, we exhort them with affection rather than authority not because we, the very last and least, acutely conscious of our lowliness, claim any right to censure license, but because we are more cautious in our solicitude and fear the devil's temptation. This caution is not empty or vain fear; it looks to the way of salvation and keeps the Lord's vital commands, so that those who have dedicated themselves to Christ, turning from carnal desire, have vowed themselves to God in body and mind alike, may complete their work destined for a great reward. They must not strive to adorn themselves or please anyone but their Lord, from whom they also expect the reward of virginity, he himself saying: "Not all can accept this word, but only those to whom it is given. For there are eunuchs who were born so from their mother's womb, and there are eunuchs who were made so by men, and there are eunuchs who made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven" (Matthew 19:12). Again, through the voice of the angels, the gift of continence is shown, virginity is proclaimed: "These are those who have not defiled themselves with women, for they remained virgins. These follow the Lamb wherever he goes" (Revelation 14:4). The Lord does not promise the grace of continence only to men and pass over women; since woman is part of man, taken and formed from him, in nearly all the Scriptures God speaks to the first-formed man, because the two are one flesh and woman is signified in the man.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A provides a faithful clause-by-clause translation. Pass B provides a polished version with necessary scripture citations (Psalm 2:12, Proverbs 3:11-12, Jeremiah 3:15, 1 Corinthians 6:19-20, John 5:14, Matthew 19:12, Revelation 14:4) which correspond correctly to the quoted or alluded content in the Latin. All theological nuances (e.g., the distinction between sinning before and after knowing God's discipline) are preserved.
